config.title: Nested Routes & Protected Routes

intro.title: Nested Routes & Protected Routes
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Vue application with a dashboard that has nested pages and a login-protected area. You will learn how to use Vue Router to create nested routes, which allow you to organize related views under a parent layout. You will also implement route guards to protect certain routes, ensuring only authenticated users can access them. By the end, you will understand how to structure complex applications and add basic authentication-based navigation.
intro.usecase: Nested and protected routes are essential for structuring complex applications with hierarchical navigation and access control. For example, in a user dashboard, nested routes allow you to organize main sections like 'Profile', 'Settings', and 'Billing', each with their own sub-pages, while protected routes ensure only authenticated users can access these areas. This pattern is common in admin panels, e-commerce sites with checkout flows, and enterprise apps where role-based permissions restrict access to specific features.

objectives: Configure nested route structures using Vue Router's children property
Implement route guards to control access to protected routes
Construct dynamic navigation components that reflect nested route hierarchies
Apply route meta fields to define authentication requirements
Initialize nested route components with proper prop passing
Render nested route views within parent route templates
Integrate authentication state with route protection logic

steps.title: Import Vue Router and create router instance
steps.instruction: Import createRouter and createWebHistory from 'vue-router' and create a basic router instance with an empty routes array.
steps.hint: You'll need to import the router creation functions and initialize a router object with history mode and routes.
steps.seedCode:
// Import Vue Router functions and create router instance

// Your code here
steps.expectedOutcome: A router instance is created with history mode and an empty routes array, ready for route definitions.
successCriteria: createRouter and createWebHistory are imported from 'vue-router', and a router instance is created with history: createWebHistory() and routes: [].
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've imported both createRouter and createWebHistory, and created the router instance with history and routes properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you're importing from 'vue-router' and creating the router with createRouter({ history: createWebHistory(), routes: [] }).

steps.title: Define parent route with children array
steps.instruction: Create a parent route object with a path property set to '/dashboard' and a children property containing an empty array for nested routes.
steps.hint: In Vue Router, nested routes are defined by adding a children array to a parent route object. Each route object needs at least a path property.
steps.expectedOutcome: A routes array containing one parent route object with path '/dashboard' and an empty children array.
successCriteria: The routes array contains a parent route object with path '/dashboard' and children array property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you have a route object with both path and children properties. The children should be an array.
steps.feedbackWrong: The parent route structure isn't quite right. You need a route object with path '/dashboard' and children array.

steps.title: Add nested child routes
steps.instruction: Inside the children array of the '/dashboard' route, add two child route objects: one with path 'profile' and component: 'DashboardProfile', and another with path 'settings' and component: 'DashboardSettings'.
steps.hint: Add objects with path and component properties to the children array. The component values should be strings matching the component names.
steps.expectedOutcome: The children array now contains two route objects with paths 'profile' and 'settings' and their respective component references.
successCriteria: The children array includes two objects: one with path 'profile' and component 'DashboardProfile', and another with path 'settings' and component 'DashboardSettings'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some child routes, but make sure you have both 'profile' and 'settings' routes with their correct component references.
steps.feedbackWrong: The children array doesn't contain the required child routes. Add two objects with path and component properties as specified.

steps.title: Create parent component with router-view
steps.instruction: Create a Vue component named Dashboard that serves as the parent layout. Inside the component, return a div element containing a heading and a router-view element for nested content.
steps.hint: Use the Vue component syntax with a template section. The router-view element will render the nested child routes.
steps.expectedOutcome: A Dashboard component is created with a template containing a heading and router-view for nested routes.
successCriteria: Dashboard component is defined with a template that includes a div, a heading, and a router-view element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your Dashboard component has a template with a div containing both a heading and a router-view element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Dashboard component is missing or incomplete. Create a Vue component with a template that includes a heading and router-view for nested content.

steps.title: Create child components for nested routes
steps.instruction: Create a Vue component named DashboardHome that returns a simple heading element with text 'Dashboard Home'.
steps.hint: Define a component that returns a template with an <h2> element containing the text.
steps.expectedOutcome: A DashboardHome component is defined that will be used as a child route component.
successCriteria: DashboardHome component is created with a template containing an <h2> with text 'Dashboard Home'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the component returns a template with an <h2> element containing 'Dashboard Home'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The DashboardHome component isn't properly defined. Create a component that returns a template with an <h2> containing 'Dashboard Home'.

steps.title: Add router-link navigation in parent component
steps.instruction: In the Dashboard component, add two router-link elements inside the nav element to navigate to the child routes: one for '/dashboard' with text 'Home' and another for '/dashboard/settings' with text 'Settings'.
steps.hint: Use the router-link component with the 'to' prop to specify the target route path.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Dashboard component will have navigation links that allow switching between the nested child routes.
successCriteria: The Dashboard component contains two router-link elements with correct 'to' props and text content.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that you have both router-link elements with the correct 'to' props and text.
steps.feedbackWrong: The navigation links aren't quite right. Make sure you're using router-link components with the 'to' prop inside the nav element.

steps.title: Create authentication state
steps.instruction: Create a reactive ref called 'isAuthenticated' to track authentication status (true/false). Initialize it with a default value of false.
steps.hint: Use Vue's ref function to create reactive state. Import ref from 'vue' if needed.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: reactive state for user
const isLoggedIn = ref(false);
steps.expectedOutcome: A reactive ref named 'isAuthenticated' is created with an initial value of false.
successCriteria: The code includes 'const isAuthenticated = ref(false);' to track authentication status.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using Vue's ref function and initializing it with false.
steps.feedbackWrong: Create a reactive ref called 'isAuthenticated' with an initial value of false.

steps.title: Create login/logout handler functions
steps.instruction: Create two functions named 'login' and 'logout' that toggle the isAuthenticated state between true and false.
steps.hint: Define these functions after the isAuthenticated ref declaration. Each function should set isAuthenticated.value to either true or false.
steps.expectedOutcome: Two handler functions are defined that can toggle the authentication state when called.
successCriteria: The code contains a 'login' function that sets isAuthenticated.value to true and a 'logout' function that sets it to false.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have both 'login' and 'logout' functions that properly set isAuthenticated.value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The required functions aren't present yet. Create both 'login' and 'logout' functions that toggle the isAuthenticated state.

steps.title: Add authentication controls to UI
steps.instruction: In your Dashboard component template, add a <div> element above the <h2> that displays the current authentication status and contains buttons to call the login and logout handlers.
steps.hint: You can display the authentication status using the isAuthenticated ref value and add buttons with @click handlers that call the login and logout functions.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding authentication UI in a Vue component template: `

Logged in: {{ isLoggedIn }}

Main Content

`
steps.expectedOutcome: The Dashboard component will display authentication status and controls above the main content.
successCriteria: The Dashboard template includes a <div> with authentication status display and buttons that call login/logout handlers.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some authentication UI elements, but make sure you have: 1) A <div> containing the authentication section, 2) Display of the current isAuthenticated value, 3) Buttons with @click handlers for both login and logout functions.
steps.feedbackWrong: The authentication controls are not properly implemented. Check that you've added a <div> above the <h2> that displays the authentication status and contains buttons with @click handlers for login and logout.

steps.title: Create route guard function
steps.instruction: Create a navigation guard function named 'requireAuth' that checks if the user is authenticated and redirects to '/login' if not.
steps.hint: Define a function that takes 'to', 'from', and 'next' parameters. Inside, check the 'isAuthenticated' ref value and call 'next()' or 'next('/login')' accordingly.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named 'requireAuth' is defined that checks authentication and redirects unauthenticated users.
successCriteria: The 'requireAuth' function is created with proper parameters, checks 'isAuthenticated.value', and calls 'next()' or 'next('/login')'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your function has all three parameters (to, from, next) and properly checks the authentication state.
steps.feedbackWrong: The route guard function isn't quite right. Check the function name, parameters, and authentication logic.

steps.title: Apply route guard to protected route
steps.instruction: Add the beforeEnter route guard to the '/dashboard' route in your routes array to protect it with your authentication check.
steps.hint: Add a beforeEnter property to the parent route object and set it to your route guard function.
steps.expectedOutcome: The '/dashboard' route will now be protected by your authentication guard function.
successCriteria: The parent route object has a beforeEnter property set to your route guard function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added the beforeEnter property to the correct route object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The route guard hasn't been applied correctly. Check that you've added beforeEnter to the '/dashboard' route object.

steps.title: Test nested navigation and route protection
steps.instruction: Add a test message to the DashboardHome component to verify it renders correctly when navigating to the nested route.
steps.hint: Add a simple paragraph or heading inside the DashboardHome component template to confirm it's working.
steps.expectedOutcome: The DashboardHome component will display a test message when you navigate to the nested route, confirming nested routing works.
successCriteria: DashboardHome component contains a visible test message in its template.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some content, but make sure it's a clear test message that will be visible when the route loads.
steps.feedbackWrong: The DashboardHome component still needs a test message to verify the nested route renders properly.
